title: Streamed per-invocation cost rollups and alert-fuzz controller to reduce noisy long-tail alerts
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: SRE runbooks show a high volume of noisy alert triggers driven by microbursty token-cost spikes from long conversational tails. This PR introduces a streamed rollup pipeline that computes lightweight per-invocation cost summaries (decibel-weighted rollups) in the telemetry ingest path and an alert-fuzz controller that applies hysteresis + probabilistic smoothing to alert evaluation to reduce churn. Key goals: 1) preserve signal for real regressions 2) suppress transient burst noise without dropping visibility 3) keep rollup compute < 2% of telemetry budget. Changes: adds a streaming aggregator service that builds three compact rollup artifacts per invocation (total_tokens, decibel_cost, tail_entropy) and attaches a rollup-hash to the trace; introduces an AlertFuzzController that hooks into the alert pipeline and rewrites thresholds by applying time-decayed fuzz envelopes and cohort-aware suppression; wires rollup metadata into the observability query layer and dashboard panels. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4211) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] E2E synthetic replay with noisy tails - [x] Backwards-compatible schema migration for rollup tags - [x] Alert playground run and tuning notes Commits are small/iterative to aid review. Related: SUP-3321 incident notes, OBS-88 spike analysis. TODO: follow-up to add tenant-level opt-out and tighten memory bounds for high-cardinality tenants.

release_notes: Add lightweight streamed per-invocation cost rollups (decibel-weighted cost, tail entropy) and an AlertFuzzController to reduce noisy long-tail alert churn. Rollups are opt-out per-tenant and attached to traces as rollup_hash tags. Includes dashboard panels and replaybench scenarios for tuning.
notes_for_ops: Deploy order: rollup aggregator binary -> feature flag on ingest -> enable AlertFuzzController in alerting config. Monitor 'rollup_ingest_error_rate' and 'alert_suppression_rate' dashboards during canary. Memory watch recommended for tenants with > 10k concurrent invocations.
